text:
For a plane electromagnetic wave, the magnetic field at a point x and time t is

$\vec{B}(x,t)$ = $\left [1.2\times 10^{-7}\sin \left (0.5\times 10^{3}x+1.5\times 10^{11}t\right )\widehat{k}\right ]$ T

The instantaneous electric field $\vec{E}$
 corresponding to $\vec{B}$
 is :

(speed of light $c = 3 × 10^{8}$
 $ms^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\vec{B}(x,t)$ = $\left [1.2\times 10^{-7}\sin \left (0.5\times 10^{3}x+1.5\times 10^{11}t\right )\widehat{k}\right ]$ T

Wave is travelling along (–x) axis and $\vec{B}$ is along
+z axis.

We know, Magnitude of electric field

E = BC

= 1.2 $\times$ $10^{-7} \sin  ( 0.5 10 + 1.5\times10^{11}t )$ $\times$ 3 $\times$ $10^{8}$

= 36 sin (0.5$\times10^{3}x+1.5\times10^{11}t) V/m$

Also, $\vec{s}=\frac{\vec{E}\times \vec{B}}{μ_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\hat{i}=\frac{\vec{E}\times \widehat{k}}{μ_{0}}$

$\therefore$ Direction of $\vec{E}=-\hat{j}$

$\therefore$ Instantaneous electric field,

 $\vec{E}(x,t)=\left [-36\sin \left (0.5\times 10^{3}x+1.5\times 10^{11}t\right )\hat{j}\right ]\frac{V}{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
Particle A of mass $m_{1}$
 moving with velocity $\left (\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right )ms^{-1}$ collides with another particle B of mass $m_{2}$
which is at rest initially. Let $\vec{V_{1}}$
 and $\vec{V_{2}}$
 be the velocities of particles A and B after collision
respectively. If $m_{1}$
 $= 2m_{2}$
 and after
 collision $\vec{V_{1}}=\left (\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}\right )$
, the angle between $\vec{V_{1}}$
 and $\vec{V_{2}}$
 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $m_{1}$
 $= 2m_{2}$

So let, $m_{2} = m$ and $m_{1} = 2m$

From momentum conservation

$\vec{p}_{i}$ = $\vec{p}_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ (2m)$\left (\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right )$ + 0 = 2m$\left (\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}\right )$ + m$\vec{V}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{V}_{2}$ = 2$\left (\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right )$ - 2$\left (\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{V}_{2}$ = $\left (2\sqrt{3}-2\right )\hat{i}-\hat{j}\left (2\sqrt{3}-2\right )$

= $2\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )\left (\hat{i}-\hat{j}\right )$

Also given after collision $\vec{V_{1}}=\left (\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}\right )ms^{-1}$

For angle between $\vec{V}_{1}$ & $\vec{V}_{2}$,

cos $θ$ = $\frac{\vec{V}_{1}.\vec{V}_{2}}{\left |\vec{V}_{1}\right |\left |\vec{V}_{2}\right |}$

= $\frac{2\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )\times 1-2\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )\times \sqrt{3}}{2\times 2\sqrt{2}\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )}$

= $\frac{2\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )\left (1-\sqrt{3}\right )}{2\times 2\sqrt{2}\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )}$

= $\frac{\left (1-\sqrt{3}\right )}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ $= 105^{o}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
When a car is at rest, its driver sees rain drops falling on it vertically. When driving the car with
speed v, he sees that rain drops are coming at an angle 60° from the horizontal. On further
increasing the speed of the car to (1 + $β$)v, this angle changes to $45^{o}$. The value of $β$ is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the car at rest the rain falls vertically, so the rain's velocity relative to the ground is vertical with some speed $v_{r}$.

The velocity of the rain relative to the car is $⃗{v}_{\text{rain}}-⃗{v}_{\text{car}}$: a vertical component $v_{r}$ downward and a horizontal component equal to the car's speed, directed opposite to the car's motion. Its angle $θ$ with the horizontal therefore satisfies $\tan θ=\dfrac{v_{r}}{v_{\text{car}}}$.

At speed $v$:

$\tan 60^{\circ }=\dfrac{v_{r}}{v}\Rightarrow v_{r}=\sqrt{3}v$

At speed $(1+β)v$:

$\tan 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{v_{r}}{(1+β)v}\Rightarrow (1+β)v=\sqrt{3}v$

$β=\sqrt{3}-1\approx 0.73$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
A charged particle going around in a circle can be considered to be a current loop. A particle of
mass m carrying charge q is moving in a plane with speed v under the influence of magnetic field $\vec{B}$.
The magnetic moment of this moving particle:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

The magnetic force provides the centripetal force:

$qvB=\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$

The revolving charge is a current $i=\dfrac{q}{T}=\dfrac{qv}{2πr}$ around the area $πr^{2}$:

$M=iπr^{2}=\dfrac{qvr}{2}=\dfrac{qv}{2}\times \dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{mv^{2}}{2B}$

For a positive charge, $q⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}$ points to the centre only when the charge circulates in the sense whose right-hand-rule normal is opposite to $⃗{B}$. A negative charge circulates the other way, but its equivalent current is again in the same sense. So $⃗{M}$ is always antiparallel to $⃗{B}$:

$⃗{M}=-\dfrac{mv^{2}}{2B}\hat{B}=-\dfrac{mv^{2}}{2B}\left (\dfrac{⃗{B}}{B}\right )=-\dfrac{mv^{2}⃗{B}}{2B^{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
A square loop of side 2$a$ and carrying current I is kept in xz plane with its centre at origin. A long
wire carrying the same current I is placed parallel to z-axis and passing through point (0, b, 0),
(b >> a). The magnitude of torque on the loop about z-axis will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]



[IMG]


First, let's consider the magnetic field created by the long wire carrying a current $I$ at a distance $b$. According to Ampere's Law, the magnetic field $B$ at a distance $b$ from a long straight wire is given by:

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}$

where $μ_{0}$ is the permeability of free space.

Given that the square loop of side $2a$ is carrying the same current $I$ and is located in the xz-plane with its center at the origin, we can analyze the forces on each side of the loop. The sides of the loop parallel to the x-axis will experience forces due to the magnetic field from the long wire. Considering symmetry and the directions of forces, the net force on these sides will not contribute to the torque around the z-axis.

The contribution to the torque around the z-axis will predominantly come from the sides of the loop parallel to the y-axis. For these sides, the magnetic forces will be in opposite directions and will create a torque around the z-axis.

Let's calculate the forces on the sides parallel to the y-axis. For a current element $Idl$ in the presence of a magnetic field $B$, the force $dF$ is given by:

$dF=Idl\times B$

For the sides at $x=a$ and $x=-a$, the distances to the wire are $a+b$ and $a-b$, respectively.

The magnetic fields at these positions due to the long wire are:

For $x=a$:

$B_{a}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2π(a+b)}$

For $x=-a$:

$B_{-a}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2π(a-b)}$

Since $b\gg a$, we can approximate these fields using binomial expansion for small $\left (\frac{a}{b}\right )$:

$B_{a}\approx \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1-\frac{a}{b}\right )$

$B_{-a}\approx \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1+\frac{a}{b}\right )$

The forces on each side of the loop with length $2a$ are:

For $x=a$:

$F_{a}=I\cdot 2a\cdot B_{a}=I\cdot 2a\cdot \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1-\frac{a}{b}\right )$

For $x=-a$:

$F_{-a}=I\cdot 2a\cdot B_{-a}=I\cdot 2a\cdot \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1+\frac{a}{b}\right )$

The net torque $τ$ around the z-axis is due to these forces, with lever arms $a$ and $-a$ respectively:

$τ=2a(F_{a}-F_{-a})$

Substituting the expressions for $F_{a}$ and $F_{-a}$:

$τ=2a\left [I\cdot 2a\cdot \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1-\frac{a}{b}\right )-I\cdot 2a\cdot \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (1+\frac{a}{b}\right )\right ]$

Simplifying this expression, we get:

$τ=2a\left [2aI\cdot \frac{μ_{0}I}{2πb}\left (-\frac{2a}{b}\right )\right ]$

$τ=-2a\cdot \frac{4a^{2}μ_{0}I^{2}}{2πb^{2}}$

The negative sign indicates the direction of the torque, but the magnitude is:

$τ=\frac{4a^{3}μ_{0}I^{2}}{πb^{2}}$

Since $a\ll b$, the approximate magnitude of the torque around the z-axis simplifies to:

$τ=\frac{2μ_{0}I^{2}a^{2}}{πb}$

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option A

$\frac{2μ_{0}I^{2}a^{2}}{πb}$

text:
The linear mass density of a thin rod AB of length L varies from A to B as

$λ(x)=λ_{0}\left (1+\frac{x}{L}\right )$,  where
x is the distance from A. If M is the mass of the rod then its moment of inertia about an axis passing
through A and perpendicular to the rod is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


dm = $λ$dx

= $λ_{0}\left (1+\frac{x}{L}\right )$dx

Integrating both side, we get

$\int\limits _{0}^{M}dm=\int\limits _{0}^{L}λ_{0}\left (1+\frac{x}{L}\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow$ M = $λ_{0}L+\frac{λ_{0}L^{2}}{2L}$ = $\frac{3λ_{0}L}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ_{0}=\frac{2M}{3L}$ .....(1)

Moment of inertia of small part dx is

dI = dmx$^{2}$

Integrating both side, we get

$\int\limits _{0}^{I}dI=\int\limits _{0}^{L}dmx^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ I = $\int\limits _{0}^{L}λ_{0}\left (1+\frac{x}{L}\right )dxx^{2}$

= $λ_{0}\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (x^{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{L}\right )dx$

= $λ_{0}\left [\frac{L^{3}}{3}+\frac{L^{3}}{4}\right ]$

= $\frac{7L^{3}λ_{0}}{12}$

Here by putting the value of $λ_{0}$ from (1)

I = $\frac{7L^{3}}{12}\left (\frac{2M}{3L}\right )$ = $\frac{7}{18}ML^{2}$

text:
Two identical electric point dipoles have dipole moments $\vec{p}_{1}=p\hat{i}$ and $\vec{p}_{2}=-p\hat{i}$ and are held on the x
axis at distance '$a$' from each other. When released, they move along the x-axis with the direction
of their dipole moments remaining unchanged. If the mass of each dipole is 'm', their speed when
they are infinitely far apart is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

With $k=\dfrac{1}{4πε_{0}}$, the field of dipole 1 at a point on its axis a distance $r$ away is $⃗{E}=\dfrac{2kp}{r^{3}}\hat{i}$.

Dipole 2, with $⃗{p}_{2}=-p\hat{i}$, has potential energy in this field

$U=-⃗{p}_{2}\cdot ⃗{E}=+\frac{2kp^{2}}{r^{3}}$

$U$ decreases as $r$ increases, so the dipoles repel and move apart along the x-axis.

The dipoles start from rest at $r=a$ and $U=0$ at infinite separation. Momentum conservation gives the two equal masses equal speeds $v$, so

$\frac{2kp^{2}}{a^{3}}=2\times \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\Rightarrow v^{2}=\frac{2p^{2}}{4πε_{0}ma^{3}}=\frac{p^{2}}{2πε_{0}ma^{3}}$

$v=\frac{p}{a}\sqrt{\frac{1}{2πε_{0}ma}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
Two planets have masses M and 16 M and their radii are $a$ and 2$a$, respectively. The separation
between the centres of the planets is 10$a$. A body of mass m is fired from the surface of the larger
planet towards the smaller planet along the line joining their centres. For the body to be able to
reach at the surface of smaller planet, the minimum firing speed needed is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let at point P, net gravitational force = 0

$\therefore$ $\frac{G(M)(m)}{(10a-x)^{2}}=\frac{G(16M)(m)}{x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 8a

By Conservation of Mechanical Energy,

$U_{i} + K_{i} = U_{f} + K_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\frac{GMm}{8a}-\frac{16GMm}{2a}$ + $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

= $-\frac{16GMm}{8a}-\frac{GMm}{2a}$ + 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$ = $GMm\left [\frac{1}{8a}+\frac{16}{2a}-\frac{1}{2a}-\frac{16}{8a}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$ = $GMm\left [\frac{1+64-4-16}{8a}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=GMm\left [\frac{45}{8a}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\sqrt{\frac{90GM}{8a}}$ = $\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{\frac{5GM}{a}}$

text:
In the figure shown, the current in the 10 V battery is close to :

[IMG]
options: 0.36 A from negative to positive terminal
0.42 A from positive to negative terminal
0.71 A from positive to negative terminal
0.21 A from positive to negative terminal
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The $5\Omega$ resistor, the 20 V cell and the $2\Omega$ resistor lie in one branch between the top junction B and the bottom junction A, so they act as a 20 V source of resistance $5+2=7\Omega$ with its positive terminal towards B.


[IMG]

Take $V_{B}=0$ and $V_{A}=x$. Three branches join A and B: the 20 V source with $7\Omega$, the $10\Omega$ resistor, and the $4\Omega$ resistor in series with the 10 V cell whose positive terminal is at B. The negative terminals of the two cells are then at $-20\text{V}$ and $-10\text{V}$.

KCL at A (sum of currents leaving A is zero):

$\dfrac{x+20}{7}+\dfrac{x+10}{4}+\dfrac{x}{10}=0$

Multiplying by 140:

$20(x+20)+35(x+10)+14x=0\Rightarrow 69x=-750\Rightarrow x=-\dfrac{250}{23}\approx -10.87\text{V}$

The current from A through the $4\Omega$ resistor towards the negative terminal of the 10 V cell is

$i=\dfrac{x-(-10)}{4}=\dfrac{-20/23}{4}=-\dfrac{5}{23}\text{A}\approx -0.22\text{A}$

The negative sign means the current leaves the negative terminal of the 10 V cell, so inside the cell about 0.22 A flows from the positive to the negative terminal, closest to 0.21 A.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
A particle moving in the xy plane experiences a velocity dependent force

$\vec{F}=k\left (v_{y}\hat{i}+v_{x}\hat{j}\right )$
, where $v_{x}$
and $v_{y}$
 are the 
x and y components of its velocity $\vec{v}$
. If $\vec{a}$
 is the
 acceleration of the particle, then

which of the following statements is true for the particle?
options: kinetic energy of particle is constant in time
$\vec{F}$ arises due to a magnetic field
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\vec{F}=k\left (v_{y}\hat{i}+v_{x}\hat{j}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ m$\vec{a}$ = $k\left (v_{y}\hat{i}+v_{x}\hat{j}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{a}=\frac{k}{m}\left (v_{y}\hat{i}+v_{x}\hat{j}\right )$

Also $\frac{dv_{x}}{dt}=\frac{k}{m}v_{y}$

and $\frac{dv_{y}}{dt}=\frac{k}{m}v_{x}$

$\frac{dv_{x}}{dv_{y}}=\frac{v_{y}}{v_{x}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\int v_{x}dv_{x}=\int v_{y}dv_{y}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{y}^{2}=v_{x}^{2}+C$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{y}^{2}-v_{x}^{2}=C$ = Constant

From Option (B),

$\vec{v}\times \vec{a}$

= $\left (v_{x}\hat{i}+v_{y}\hat{j}\right )\times \frac{k}{m}\left (v_{y}\hat{i}+v_{x}\hat{j}\right )$

= $\left (v_{x}^{2}\widehat{k}-v_{y}^{2}\widehat{k}\right )\times \frac{k}{m}$

= $\left (v_{x}^{2}-v_{y}^{2}\right )\times \frac{k}{m}\widehat{k}$

= Constant

text:
A Young's double-slit experiment is performed using monochromatic light of wavelength $λ$. The
intensity of light at a point on the screen, where the path difference is $λ$, is K units. The intensity
of light at a point where the path difference is $\frac{λ}{6}$ is given by $\frac{nK}{12}$, where n is an integer. The value
of n is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $1^{st}$ case,

$\Delta𝜙$ = $\frac{2π}{λ}\times λ$ = 2$π$

$\therefore$ $I_{$net} = 4Icos$^{2}$ $\frac{\Delta 𝜙}{2}$ = 4I = K (Given)

From $2^{nd}$ case,

$\Delta𝜙$ = $\frac{2π}{λ}\times \frac{λ}{6}$ = $\frac{π}{3}$

$\therefore$ $I_{$net$} = 4I \cos ^{2}$ $\frac{\Delta 𝜙}{2}$

= 4I $\times$ $\frac{3}{4}$ = $\frac{3}{4}K$

$\therefore$ According to question,

$\frac{nK}{12}$ = $\frac{3}{4}K$

$\Rightarrow$ n = 9

text:
The centre of mass of solid hemisphere of radius 8 cm is x from the centre of the flat surface. Then
value of x is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As we know c.o.m. of hemisphere = $\frac{3R}{8}$

$\therefore$ x = $\frac{3R}{8}$ =  $\frac{3\times 8}{8}$ = 3 cm

text:
In a series LR circuit, power of 400W is dissipated from a source of 250 V, 50 Hz. The power factor
of the circuit is 0.8. In order to bring the power factor to unity, a capacitor of value C is added in
series to the L and R. Taking the value of C as $\left (\frac{n}{3π}\right )$ $μ$F,  then value of n is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the LR circuit, $P=V_{\text{rms}}I_{\text{rms}}\cos 𝜙=\dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}^{2}}{Z}\cos 𝜙$:

$400=\dfrac{(250)^{2}\times 0.8}{Z}\Rightarrow Z=125\Omega$

$R=Z\cos 𝜙=125\times 0.8=100\Omega$ and $X_{L}=\sqrt{Z^{2}-R^{2}}=\sqrt{125^{2}-100^{2}}=75\Omega$.

The power factor becomes 1 when the series capacitor cancels the inductive reactance, $X_{C}=X_{L}=75\Omega$:

$C=\dfrac{1}{2πfX_{C}}=\dfrac{1}{2π\times 50\times 75}\text{F}=\dfrac{10^{6}}{7500π}μ\text{F}=\dfrac{400}{3π}μ\text{F}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{n}{3π}μ\text{F}$ gives $n=400$.

Hence, the answer is 400.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot
